column1: # THE CANDIDATE IDENTITY TABLE, BOUND TO THE LIVE SOURCE BYTES.
# Every range below was MEASURED from the live source with
#   MODE=RANGE    recompute the SHA-256 of an exact source line range
#   MODE=IDENTITY validate the whole table against the live census
# THE CORRECTION OF THE RECON05 RANGES (A REAL, MATERIAL FINDING)
# RECON05's candidate ranges were recorded from the CENSUS tool's
# `body_line`, which is the END OF THE FUNCTION'S OWN TRAILING COMMENT
# BLOCK, not the end of the function body.  For 10 of the 12 scalar
# candidates this makes the recorded range SPAN PAST the candidate's
# own closing brace and INTO the next function's body.
# The consequence is that SEVEN RECON05 candidate ranges OVERLAP each
# other, and THREE of them contain ANOTHER CANDIDATE'S ENTIRE BODY:
# The nine overlapping pairs under the RECON05 ranges were:
# The canonical verifier does NOT detect these: its
# OVERLAPPING_IDENTITY check only compares rows that resolve to WHOLE
# FUNCTIONS in the live census, and these candidate ranges do not
# (they are sub-decisions inside a larger function body).
# WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE SELECTION: a range that contains another
# candidate's body cannot be the source-binding for a bounded
# ABI.  A PolyC component migrated from that range would, by
# construction, also own the OTHER candidate's decision.  The
# fact would be measured over the WRONG bytes.
# RECON07 THEREFORE RECORDS THE TIGHT, FUNCTION-BODIED RANGES ABOVE.
# The RECON05 ranges are PRESERVED UNCHANGED in the historical evidence
# tree (F14).  This ACT does not edit any historical artifact.
# UNDER THE RECON07 TIGHT RANGES: 0 overlapping pairs.
# THE TWO FROZEN HISTORICAL RANGES THAT ARE ALREADY TIGHT
